text: The case status, the task and the timer stay rwb-case's. The release branch reports an outcome to the parent CaseWorkflow, which moves the case to PLAN_COMPLETED, to COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED, to CASE_CLOSED_SETTLED or to ASSET_ON_BOOKS per the rule, closes the treatment and raises any unmatched task. No case, task or timer table is read or written by rwb-treatment, and the message shown while a release is requested and not confirmed is a screen text of that outcome.
why: Three of the four rules that drive the release end with the case in a new state (PLAN_COMPLETED, COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED, CASE_CLOSED_SETTLED, ASSET_ON_BOOKS) and AC2 ends with 'the case moves to PLAN_COMPLETED', while Architecture v5 slide 13 gives rwb-treatment no call to P3, DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables, rwb-case owns the case, its queues, tasks and timers, and no source states the text shown while a release is open.

text: The four views are this service's own read-only ACE views: v_ace_account, v_ace_payment, v_ace_collateral and v_ace_collateral_detail are granted SELECT to the login of rwb-treatment, the legacy in_active fact and the zero-balance and installment facts are columns of that read, and no release status is derived in code from lien_rank or register_date. The CCMS result arrives as the fact ACE ingests and this service re-reads; no live CCMS call and no live Land Office call is published. If the platform keeps the views to rwb-source-data, the read moves to that contract and a C dependency appears.
why: DP-05 allows either the contract read of rwb-source-data or the service's own views and the Work Package lists no C dependency, while the two facts AC1 conditions on, the zero balance and the in_active value, are named by no view field in the source and the architecture says the recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data.

text: The release answer is published as an optional collateralRelease section of the treatment answer of RWB-S2-E3001-CON at the same major version, with the properties releaseStatus, requestRef, requestedAt, releasedAt, checkedAt, collateralCount, collateralNo, assetKey, ruleId and ruleVersion, and the five answer states of the contract vocabulary. The R-RES-33 comparison is made on installments (DF-TRT-009) and installments_paid (DF-TRT-032). The names, the example values and the error mapping are the working read; no table, no column and no code list is created by them. The settlement clearance and the confirmation limit are values in force whose names and numbers no source gives, and the interval of the confirmation read is the working read.
why: No source gives the release result a field, an element or an operation, the legacy story lists only the treatment create and the treatment read, TSD S2 T3.1 carries no installments_due field although R-RES-33 conditions on one, and the clearance event that starts R-SET-20 has no catalogue row, so these values have to be published somewhere for five consumers to build against.

text: The release instruction leaves this service as the event rwb.treatment.CollateralReleaseRequested.v1 on rwb.treatment.events.v1, written to the outbox in the same transaction as the change, and the adapter that delivers it to CCMS (INT-10) is platform and rwb-integration work: it subscribes to the event, owns the transport and the file or message format, and reports its result to the outbox. No call from rwb-treatment to CCMS and no C dependency is recorded, because the Work Package lists none and the connection matrix gives rwb-treatment no cell to P2 or to Outside. The parameter values of the event and the transport are the working read.
why: The legacy story says the release 'leaves through the outbound interface to CCMS' and the target forbids a service from calling a source system directly, while Architecture v5 slide 13 gives rwb-treatment no cell to P2 rwb-integration and none to Outside, the event catalogue has no release event, and the Work Package records no C and no X dependency for the pair.
